scope: Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core; standard 16-space, 12-turn, 2–4-player multiplayer; base objective deck; Universal Rules Compendium plus Corrigendum 1.0. Marked expansions and optional modes excluded.
assessment: No material rules error or important omission found. Quantities, costs, timing, destinations, exceptions, objective requirements, scoring and ending/tie conditions were checked independently against the permitted primary sources.

source_review.reviewed_compendium_sections: Base setup pp.8–12; complete base play/courtship/scoring pp.16–24; complete relevant base detailed rules pp.26–30 and 35–42; FAQ pp.76–79; base family and gentry entries pp.80, 83–85; all unmarked base improvements pp.86–104; VP cards p.105; all Base-labelled objectives pp.106–111.
source_review.direct_pdf_checks: Corrigendum both pages; compendium pp.12, 99, 104, including visual inspection of the standard round-track image on p.12; French rulebook pp.7 and 14.
source_review.supplemental_source_limit: Used only for the unchanged maximum-level reputation objective; no gameplay or seasonal flow imported from the French rulebook.

checked_claims.detail: Standard base/core multiplayer, four seasons, twelve ordinary player turns, courtship events without player turns; marked expansions and optional variants are excluded.
source_refs: Universal Rules Compendium pp.6–7, 16, 21, 76; source expansion labels throughout appendices.

checked_claims.detail: Random first player; family choice starts to that player’s left; 1.1 baseline with Cavendish at 1.4; starting servants, tiles, family, starter guest recycling, five objectives, and all four family bonuses agree.

Hire pool of one valet and maid per player, two footmen per player and two underbutlers; unused servants excluded; one double-sided monument per player plus one, at most one Estate monument; conversion suites remain in bag.
Six distinct eligible market tiles, duplicate stacks, sorting, normal/hybrid orientation, PR limit and exclusions, standard board, reminder tokens, revealed theme and base Fairchilds agree.
source_refs: Compendium pp.11–12; PDF p.12 board illustration.

checked_claims.detail: Rotation, event then ongoing effects, exact invitation counts, complete staffing, positive before negative favours, purchase and cleanup with only last player advancing agree.
Full servant and gentry recovery, event/ongoing effects, choice of £200 or market refresh, purchase and expending used servants agree; hiring when passing is excluded correctly.
Village Fair 3/9, objectives 6, Builders’ Holiday 11, National Holiday 14 and courtship 4/8/12/16 agree; events precede ongoing effects on both hosting and passing turns.
source_refs: Compendium pp.17–18, 21; direct visual inspection of standard Alderley Hall board image in PDF p.12.

checked_claims.detail: Five increments per level, minimum 1.1, maximum Max.5, Max=7 standard, and screening fixed after step 2 agree; later special-action spending does not invalidate activity eligibility.
Borrow £100 for two increments, Service Help from Quarters for three, refresh for four once per turn, repeatability of the first two, and immediate spending of excess reputation agree.
Public and unlimited supply, no interplayer transfers, affordability, use of positive favours/cards/borrowing for paupers, and minimum-reputation handling agree.

Unique/common distinction, housekeeper substitution only without available maids, Brushing Room substitution only without available valets, and underbutler’s unrestricted substitution for base male types agree.

Butler’s Room hosts without gentry, hires up to two eligible servants for no money or recruits one common servant after upgrading; new hires go to Expended Service; underbutler only via pantry and cannot be recruited.

Ordinary one-space rotation, the separate one-servant direct-use Quarters ability, repeated paid Service Help and all-servant Refresh Service are distinguished accurately; pantry hire normally takes two subsequent rotations to become available.

No hand limit; cards remain owned in discard; exact attendee types; newly acquired guests enter hand; screening reveals only kept guests; optional dismissal from hand/activity/discard to deck bottom and family immunity agree.
Lord, Lady, Heir, Young Lady and Asquith Dowager favours, choices and VP match all five base family entries.

Base Charles/Elizabeth service, favours, prestige status, absence of PR and eight VP agree; Charles qualifies for Young Lady’s male prestige guest condition; no family dismissal immunity is stated for Fairchild guests; Perkins/Oliver reputation effects agree.
Mandatory first-use upgrades, no purchase flip, repeat hybrid flips with only face-up category counting, and later-turn monument income agree.
Servants’ Hall activation and expended servant, Barn’s Estate-activity trigger, and upgraded Private Study’s Village-Fair-only reward agree.

Heritage doubles all favours including negatives; Queen’s doubles one chosen favour; Lionheart draws its guest with no personal service and doubles nonnegative favours; the latter two become monuments; fixed count one applies to all.

checked_claims.claim: Main Library and base West Terrace
checked_claims.detail: Library’s unupgraded objective draw and upgraded VP draw/counts agree. Base West Terrace remains an activity requiring three family and a butler on both sides, then prestige invitation with optional one-to-four dismissal on its upgraded side.

Read all unmarked base entries in the improvement appendix against the summary’s printed-requirement rule; explicit Long Gallery count reduction, South Lawn family requirement and base hybrid identities agree.
source_refs: Compendium pp.86–104, unmarked base entries only.

checked_claims.detail: One tile per ordinary turn unless applicable exception, Market/Reserve modifier, £100 minimum, any-reputation purchasing and absolute no-duplicate rule agree.

Slide then draw, stack duplicates, no refill for a surviving stack, sort only newly drawn tiles, seasonal service/PR1 Reserve routing, Largest Wine Cellar exception and public choice of any Reserve tile agree.
Set market aside, refill six before returning old tiles, unchanged Reserve, multiple independent VP-card refreshes, and single unchanged market/prices for Holiday or Market Purchase purchases agree.
Required default refresh after each of first three courtships and upkeep order are accurate for the selected compendium; older player aid is explicitly superseded on this point.
source_refs: Compendium p.23; Corrigendum 1.0 p.2, Player Aid Note.

checked_claims.detail: Five starting plus two event objectives, one discard each courtship, secret bottom-deck discards, three normally retained, extra objectives increasing retained count and ownership without upgrading agree.
Benefit-or-VP choice, immediate/later-own-turn/final usage, bottom-deck used cards and all ten listed types’ effects agree, including family recovery and excluding underbutler hires.

Return Fairchilds first, face-up theme tile VP including negatives, tied winners’ VP cards, objective discard, final sum of all four themes, repeated category double count and level-only final tie break agree.
All seven scoring categories, 1/3/6/10/15/21/28 reputation schedule, two VP per servant, £200 per VP rounded down, final Fairchild and level-only tie breaks agree.

Checked the ten group objectives, two guest bonuses, five category bonuses, six servant bonuses, four individual tiles, reputation, monument and wealth bonuses against entries marked Base; point values and requirements agree.

Monuments remain in printed categories; upgraded Queen’s/Lionheart count both for their category and monument objectives; hybrids count only face-up side; common-only basic servant objective is distinguished from general service VP.

The supplemental primary rulebook explicitly describes completion at maximum reputation level shown by the Max counter; it identifies that counter as level seven in standard play. This supports the FAQ clarification independently of the 7.5 storage maximum.
source_refs: Super Meeple official French base rulebook PDF pp.7, 14, and matching supplied text; Compendium pp.27, 111.

independence_statement: This was a fresh audit of the supplied summary snapshot against only the explicitly permitted authoritative text/PDFs and the limited supplemental primary source. I did not read questions, answer keys, reader responses, grades, earlier audits or other QA files; did not communicate with readers; did not assume a previous verdict; and did not edit or repair the summary. The only saved audit artifact is this JSON file.
